Writers mutate (so not safe) but must be repeatable (idempotent); readers must not mutate (safe) and therefore are trivially idempotent.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If at-least-once delivery only affects the write path (not reads), the reader-side safety claim is vacuous.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log permits readers to trigger side effects (e.g., consumer-offset commits), readers are not safe either.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At-least-once delivery applies to both read and write paths in distributed logs. On the write path, idempotence via deduplication keys is the minimal requirement because safety would forbid writes. On the read path, safety suffices and implies idempotence for free. The causal mechanism is the split of the log protocol into a mutation channel (writer\u2192log, idempotent) and an observation channel (reader\u2190log, safe). This maps to RFC 9110's separation of methods into those that change state (PUT, POST, DELETE) and those that don't (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
